canonical.title: Windows to Linux in 2026: what crosses over, what doesn't, and how to stage the switch

parent.title: Which Linux to switch to in 2026: a decision framework for a .NET developer leaving Windows

siblings.title: The 2026 Linux distro landscape: what actually differs between the families
siblings.summary: There are only five real distro families, and for a Windows developer moving to Linux in 2026 the honest shortlist is Fedora Workstation, Ubuntu LTS, Linux Mint, Bluefin/Aurora, and openSUSE Tumbleweed — everything else is a variation, a server OS, or a hobby.

siblings.title: Stable, rolling, or atomic: picking a release model for your first Linux daily driver
siblings.summary: Start on a 6-month fixed release (Fedora Workstation) or an atomic Fedora image (Bluefin DX); avoid pure rolling and avoid Debian stable.

siblings.title: Toolchain fit: which Linux distro costs least setup work for .NET 10 + TypeScript + Docker in 2026
siblings.summary: For a .NET 10 + TypeScript + Docker workstation in 2026, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS and Fedora 44 tie on setup effort and every other family costs you at least one hand-configured vendor repo.

siblings.title: Picking a Linux desktop in 2026: the Windows 11 switcher's decision guide
siblings.summary: KDE Plasma is the lowest-friction landing spot for a Windows 11 developer in 2026; X11 sessions die this year.

siblings.title: Hardware and driver reality in 2026: only three things should decide your distro
siblings.summary: In 2026 only three hardware classes still force a distro choice — NVIDIA, very new silicon, and Secure-Boot dual-boot; everything else is a live-USB check away.

siblings.title: Linux upkeep in 2026: support windows, upgrade pain, and monthly chores ranked
siblings.summary: Atomic Fedora and Ubuntu/Mint LTS are near-zero chore; Fedora Workstation costs one upgrade a year; Arch costs a reading habit you cannot skip.

siblings.title: Gaming and media on Linux in 2026: singleplayer is solved, anti-cheat and DRM streaming are not
siblings.summary: Roughly 90% of Windows Steam titles launch under Proton; the two real losses are kernel anti-cheat multiplayer and browser DRM streaming above 720p SDR.

sources.title: What's happening to Azure Data Studio
sources.claim: Azure Data Studio retired 28 February 2026; VS Code + MSSQL extension is the replacement, but SQL Server Agent and full administration remain in Windows-only SSMS.

sources.title: Quickstart: run SQL Server container images with Docker
sources.claim: SQL Server containers are supported on Linux hosts with Intel/AMD x86-64 CPUs; emulation layers are not supported.

sources.title: Microsoft Office on Linux
sources.claim: Microsoft 365 desktop apps are supported only on Windows and macOS; the web version in a browser is the supported route on Linux.

sources.title: Office 365 web vs computer program
sources.claim: Office for the web lacks VBA, third-party add-ins and offline use, and degrades on large or complex files.

sources.title: Thunderbird adds native Microsoft Exchange email support
sources.claim: Thunderbird 145 adds native Exchange over EWS with OAuth2 for M365, but calendar, contacts and Microsoft Graph are not implemented.

sources.title: Rider vs Visual Studio
sources.claim: Rider runs on Linux and covers .NET development, but has no visual designers for WPF or WinForms.

sources.title: Why is it not possible to use the eID with snap and/or Flatpak?
sources.claim: The Belgian eID cannot be used with Snap or Flatpak software because sandbox confinement blocks the PKCS#11 module.

sources.title: LibreOffice vs OnlyOffice
sources.claim: OnlyOffice uses OOXML as its native internal format giving better .docx/.xlsx fidelity, and uses JavaScript macros rather than VBA.

sources.title: ONLYOFFICE/DesktopEditors
sources.claim: OnlyOffice Desktop Editors is the open-source cross-platform office suite with native Linux builds.

sources.title: LibreOffice VBA support option
sources.claim: LibreOffice offers only partial VBA support via a compatibility option and a macro converter.

sources.title: Retirement of Teams desktop app on Linux
sources.claim: Microsoft retired the dedicated Teams desktop client for Linux in December 2022 in favour of the PWA.

sources.title: Microsoft Teams PWA now available on Linux
sources.claim: The Teams PWA is available only in Edge and Chrome on Linux.

sources.title: Screen sharing on Ubuntu is not working (Teams PWA)
sources.claim: Teams screen sharing on Linux is the recurring failure point, tied to Wayland/PipeWire portal configuration.

sources.title: Thunderbird 145 finally adds native Exchange support
sources.claim: Independent coverage confirming Thunderbird 145's native Exchange support and its limits.

sources.title: Introducing EWSAllowedAppIds: final phase of EWS retirement
sources.claim: Microsoft begins blocking EWS in Exchange Online on 1 October 2026 with full retirement in April 2027.

sources.title: JetBrains free non-commercial licensing FAQ
sources.claim: Rider is free for non-commercial use; commercial use still requires a paid licence.

sources.title: WPF and WinForms on macOS and Linux
sources.claim: WPF and WinForms applications only run on Windows; EnableWindowsTargeting permits building on Linux but not running or designing.

sources.title: SQL Server Management Studio alternatives
sources.claim: DBeaver and Beekeeper Studio are the leading cross-platform SSMS alternatives.

sources.title: PowerShell 101: working with WMI
sources.claim: The WMI cmdlets were removed in PowerShell 6+, and the CIM cmdlets that replaced them were never ported to non-Windows.

sources.title: Photopea is the closest free Photoshop replacement
sources.claim: Photopea has the best PSD compatibility of the free Photoshop alternatives; GIMP and Krita cover photo editing and illustration natively.

sources.title: Affinity (software)
sources.claim: Canva acquired Affinity in 2024 and moved it to a free unified app in 2025, with native releases for Windows and macOS only.

sources.title: Run Affinity on Linux via an unofficial AppImage
sources.claim: An unofficial Affinity v3 AppImage bundles Wine so Canva's Affinity suite runs on Ubuntu.

sources.title: seapear/AffinityOnLinux
sources.claim: AffinityOnLinux provides community install paths for Affinity via Wine, Bottles, Lutris or Heroic.

sources.title: OpenConnect
sources.claim: OpenConnect implements Cisco AnyConnect, Palo Alto GlobalProtect, F5 Big-IP and Fortinet FortiGate SSL VPN protocols on Linux.

sources.title: yuezk/GlobalProtect-openconnect
sources.claim: A GlobalProtect VPN client for Linux with SSO, MFA and YubiKey support.

sources.title: Linux eID software installation
sources.claim: Belgian eID middleware ships official packages for Debian, Ubuntu LTS, Mint, Fedora, RHEL and openSUSE Leap.

sources.title: itsme — get started
sources.claim: itsme is activated through a Belgian bank app or with an eID plus card reader.

sources.title: Office under Wine compatibility notes
sources.claim: Office 2016 and older work partially under Wine; Office 365/2021/2024 do not work reliably.

sources.title: Contain your Windows apps inside Linux
sources.claim: WinApps and WinBoat run a managed Windows VM and export individual app windows over RemoteApp/RDP.

sources.title: GPU passthrough with virt-manager, QEMU and KVM
sources.claim: KVM with virt-manager supports real PCI/VFIO passthrough and VirtIO drivers with low overhead.

sources.title: Single-GPU passthrough on a VM
sources.claim: Single-GPU passthrough hands the GPU to the VM, taking the host desktop offline for the duration.

sources.title: End-user access to a Cloud PC
sources.claim: A Windows 365 Cloud PC is reachable from any HTML5 browser, so no Linux client is needed.

sources.title: Windows 365 licensing guide
sources.claim: Windows 365 Business runs roughly $28-$56 per user per month after a 20% cut effective 1 May 2026.

sources.title: Windows Extended Security Updates
sources.claim: Windows 10 support ended 14 October 2025; consumer ESU runs until the programme ends 12 October 2027.

sources.title: 2026 dual-boot Windows and Linux setup guide
sources.claim: Windows 11 24H2 can auto-enable BitLocker even on Home; suspend BitLocker and disable Fast Startup before repartitioning.

sources.title: Dual boot with Windows (Arch Wiki)
sources.claim: A shared EFI System Partition can be damaged by hibernating one OS then booting the other; install Windows first, never reformat the ESP.

sources.title: EFI System Partition size guide
sources.claim: The ESP should be at least 260 MiB to guarantee correct FAT32 formatting.

sources.title: Fixing wrong time in dual boot
sources.claim: Windows reads the hardware clock as local time while Linux writes UTC, causing recurring clock skew.

sources.title: Linux NTFS driver reliability
sources.claim: The in-kernel ntfs3 driver has caused freezes and disk corruption; ntfs-3g is slower but stable.

sources.title: exFAT
sources.claim: exFAT has native read-write support in the Linux kernel but carries no POSIX permissions or extended attributes.

sources.title: Dropbox drops all Linux filesystems except unencrypted ext4
sources.claim: Dropbox on Linux supports only unencrypted ext4 for the sync folder because it relies on extended attributes.

sources.title: Dropbox desktop app for Linux
sources.claim: The Dropbox Linux client requires libappindicator and a desktop environment that supports AppIndicator.

sources.title: WSL2 vs native Linux developer experience
sources.claim: Container startup is ~0.3s native vs ~1.2s on WSL2 and container filesystem operations are 3-5x faster natively.

sources.title: Managing native Linux vs WSL 1/2
sources.claim: WSL2 networking defaults to NAT and is isolated from the host network stack.
